# Seed library, autumn notes

Written by Hana, 4 November.

The seed library lives in the old cloakroom at Millbrook Library, next to the large print shelf. We have 212 packets in the drawers, mostly beans, peas, lettuce, tomatoes and calendula. About 60 of those came from the Allotment Society's swap in September. The rest were donated by members over two years.

Who uses it: the allotment holders at Brook Lane (about 25 of them, some growing for 30 years) take most of the packets and bring back saved seed. Since the new flats on Ferry Road opened we also get people who have never grown anything. Six of them asked at the desk last month what a "heritage" bean is and how you get seed from a plant. The primary school's gardening club also borrows packets in spring, usually 10 to 15 at a time.

What we have to use: the community room on Thursdays, 6.30 to 8.00 pm, free from 12 February to 12 March (five Thursdays). Seats 20 at tables. A projector, a sink, two trestle tables and a seed-cleaning sieve set. Paper envelopes and labels are in the cupboard. The garden plot behind the library is 4 beds, dug over but empty until April.

Budget: £60 from the Friends of the Library for materials. Tea and coffee are free from the library kitchen.

Tom from the Allotment Society said he could come and show one session if we ask early. Nasreen, our volunteer who did a master gardener course, can do any other Thursday.
